translationRepairs: So Jumong left Buyeo with Wuyin, Wuwei, and two companions and fled southeast.
So Jumong left Buyeo with Wuyin and Wuwei and fled southeast.
等二人 totals the two immediately named companions, Wuyin and Wuwei; it does not add two unnamed people.
In the fourth year of Jianguo, Murong Yuansun marched against him by way of Nanyang, defeated him at Mudi, swept on in pursuit, and entered Wandu while Chao fled alone on horseback.

In the fourth year of Jianguo, Murong Yuanzhen marched against him by way of the southern pass (Nanxia), defeated him at Mudi, swept on in pursuit, and entered Wandu while Chao fled alone on horseback.
The source names 慕容元真 and says the force entered from 南陝; neither supports Yuansun or Nanyang.
In the fourth year of Jianguo, Murong Yuansun led troops to attack him, entering from Nanyang, fought at Mudi, routed Chao's army, pursued at length, entered Wandu, and Chao fled alone on horseback.
In the fourth year of Jianguo, Murong Yuanzhen led troops to attack him, entering from Nanxia, fought at Mudi, routed Chao's army, pursued at length, entered Wandu, and Chao fled alone on horseback.
The literal field must preserve the same source readings: 元真 is Yuanzhen and 南陝 is Nanxia, not Yuansun or Nanyang.
Mencius was praised for humanity yet did not spare the insulter on the highway.
Lord Mengchang was praised for humanity yet did not spare the insulter on the highway.
孟常 is the text's Lord Mengchang allusion, not the philosopher Mencius (孟子).
In the seventeenth year they sent the envoy Ren Pofei and more than five hundred others to present tribute.
In the seventeenth year they sent the envoy Pofei and more than five hundred others to present tribute.
使人 is the ordinary envoy construction; the personal name begins with 婆非 and has no Ren surname.
